content.text:
Your landing page is a static site that Caddy serves on the VM (`deploy/Caddyfile`, `LANDING_ADDRESS`). It sets no Content-Security-Policy, so any of these options is just a script tag in `landing/index.html`.

One thing up front: none of these tell you who a visitor is. They give you country, referrer, device and browser, pages viewed, time on page, and any clicks you choose to track. The only people you can name are the ones who sign in to the app, and they're already in your `users` table.

## Options

**1. Cookieless, privacy-first tools (my recommendation)**
These don't need a cookie banner under GDPR, which matters if you or your visitors are in the EU.
- **Umami, self-hosted.** Free and open source. It can use the Postgres you already run, as a separate database, so it's one extra lightweight container in `deploy/compose.yml` plus a Caddy route. You can also serve it from your own domain, so ad blockers don't drop it, and those blockers otherwise hide a large share of a technical audience.
- **Plausible.** A hosted service at about $9/month, or a self-hosted Community Edition that needs ClickHouse, which is heavy for your VM.
- **Cloudflare Web Analytics.** Free, and just a beacon script; your DNS doesn't have to be on Cloudflare. It's the most basic option, with no custom events worth mentioning.
- **GoatCounter.** Free hosted for non-commercial use, and very simple.

**2. Behaviour tools: heatmaps and session replay**
These come closest to "how they use it": where people click, how far they scroll, and recordings of real visits.
- **Microsoft Clarity.** Free heatmaps and recordings.
- **PostHog.** A free tier of 1M events a month, with replay, funnels and heatmaps.
- The catch for both: they use cookies, and recording visits needs consent in the EU, so you'd have to add a consent banner.

**3. Google Analytics 4**
Free and the most detailed, but it needs a consent banner in the EU. A lot of visitors decline it or block it, so your numbers come out skewed. It's overkill for a single page.

**4. Caddy access logs plus GoAccess**
No JavaScript at all. It reads the server logs Caddy already writes and shows visits, referrers and user agents. It's noisy from bots and tells you nothing about what people do on the page.

## What I'd do
Self-host Umami next to your existing Postgres, served from the landing domain. On top of page views, I'd track a few custom events that answer "how":
- clicks on the sign-in/CTA button;
- play and pause on the demo fight;
- how far people scroll, as section-reached events.

If you later want recordings, add Clarity together with a consent banner.

Do you want me to set up Umami, which touches the compose file, the Caddyfile, `index.html` and the deploy README? Or would you rather start with a hosted option like Plausible or Cloudflare, which only needs the script tag?
I don't want to trigger any consent banners. But I want a free serivice

content.text:
I've set the landing page up with **Umami Cloud's free Hobby plan**. Umami doesn't use cookies, so no consent banner is needed, and you get page views, referrers, countries, devices and custom events. The free plan is capped at about 100K events a month and keeps data for 6 months. Two catches: each stored event property counts as an extra event against that cap, and sources disagree on whether the free plan covers 1 website or 3, which only matters if you also want to track the app.

The other free options with no banner were Cloudflare Web Analytics, which only counts page views, and GoatCounter. I went with Umami because it's the only one of the three that also tracks clicks, which is what tells you how people use the page.

**What gets tracked**
- **Sign-in clicks**, tagged with which button was used: `nav`, `hero` or `final`. This tells you which call to action works.
- **How far people scroll**: a `section` event fires the first time someone reaches each section (`fight`, `method`, `live`, `start`).
- **The demo**: `replay-play` / `replay-pause`, `log-seek` (clicking a strike in the log) and `round-filter`, which records the round picked.

I checked it in the preview: every event fired with the right name and property, and there were no console errors. The script never loads on localhost, so your own testing won't count.

**Your step:** create an Umami Cloud account and add the landing domain as a website. Then paste the website ID into `UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID` in [index.html](landing/index.html). While that's empty the script doesn't load, so it's safe to deploy as is. After that it goes live with your next push to `release`.

Some visitors run ad blockers that block `cloud.umami.is`, so your numbers will undercount them. Routing the script through Caddy on your own domain would fix that, but I left it out to keep this simple.

I also added a rule to [landing/CLAUDE.md](landing/CLAUDE.md): analytics must stay cookieless and keep to one property per event. Nothing is committed.

Sources:
- [Umami Cloud FAQ](https://umami.is/docs/cloud/faq)
- [freetier.co: Umami](https://freetier.co/directory/products/umami)
- [Cloudzy Umami review](https://cloudzy.com/cs/blog/umami-review/)

content.text:
No, it doesn't need to be a secret. The website ID is public: it's sent in plain sight in your page's HTML to every visitor's browser. It can only send events to your site; it can't read your stats or touch your account.

The only thing someone could do with it is send fake events to your dashboard, and keeping it in a secret wouldn't stop that, because the ID is in the HTML anyway. The things to keep private are your Umami login and any API key, if you ever create one.

I've set the ID in [index.html:25](landing/index.html:25). You don't need to paste your `<script>` tag as well, because the existing loader adds it with your ID, except on localhost. Tracking starts once you commit this and push to `release`.
